newsitem.title: FRANCE: EMU inconceivable without Italy - France's Jospin.
newsitem.headline: EMU inconceivable without Italy - France's Jospin.

text.p: French Socialist party leader Lionel Jospin said on Tuesday it was inconceivable that a single European currency be launched without Italy.

"The membership of Italy, but also of Spain, Portugal, and Britain if it wants it, in the founding members of the single currency seems to be more and more of a crucial question," he told a news conference called to present his opposition party's social and economic policies for parliamentary elections due in March 1998.
"My view on this point is becoming stronger and stronger -- the single currency cannot be considered without Italy," he said.
Recent opinion polls have shown the Socialists could be within striking distance of a parliamentary election victory.
But even if they won control of parliament, conservative President Jacques Chirac would remain in office and continue to oversee foreign policy.

The government has declined all comment on speculation about Italian membership of monetary union, saying only that a decision will be made in early 1998 on which countries join a single currency when it is first launched in 1999.
Jospin said it would be wrong to refuse entry to countries whose people were making exceptional efforts to be ready for monetary union in January 1, 1999.
"And what would be the consequences of an Italian currency once more free to follow a policy of competitive devaluations outside the single currency?" Jospin added.
He also reiterated support for an "economic government" to coordinate economic policies inside monetary union and act as a counterbalance to the future European Central Bank.
"Everyone knows very well today that the dogmatism of central banks is an obstacle to growth.

"That is why I continue to believe that an economic government capable of setting exchange rate policy, representing monetary union, and following more ambitious policies for Europe must be set up opposite the European Central Bank," he said.
The French government has called for a special "stability council" to oversee economic policy inside the euro-zone after the launch of monetary union.

But though the idea is gaining grudging acceptance from France's European Union partners, ministers from other countries have stripped the council of most of its powers even before it is set up, notably insisting it will have no role in setting foreign exchange policy.
Jospin also said he was against any delay in monetary union.
